10179.title: Gunmen kill seven on bus in Syria’s Homs province

whatHappened.text: Gunmen opened fire on a civilian bus in western Syria’s Homs province, killing at least seven people, according to state media.
The attack happened on Wednesday as the bus crossed the Masyaf bridge in Homs, and Sana said “unknown assailants” attacked the bus and killed and wounded people.
Sana also said security forces opened an investigation and published photographs of officers examining the small bus.
The bus shooting came hours after an explosion and fire at a gas pipeline near Damascus forced three power plants offline.

whyItMatters.text: The attack highlighted security challenges for Syria’s authorities and drew a promise of accountability and pursuit of the perpetrators by internal security.

The earlier pipeline blast that preceded the bus shooting also disrupted electricity supply, with the Syrian Electricity Company warning it would increase power rationing hours due to dwindling electricity supplies.

10204.title: US forces quit Iraq after more than two decades

whatHappened.text: Iraqis celebrated the departure of US forces after more than two decades of war on Wednesday, as the withdrawal of the final troops ended the biggest US war of the century.
The final troops were withdrawn mainly from an airbase in Erbil in Iraq’s semi-autonomous Kurdish region.
Iraqi troops paraded in Baghdad and Najaf to mark the pullout.

whyItMatters.text: Many feared that the exit could create a security vacuum that increases the power of Iran-backed militias or provides an opening for the return of Islamic State.

The Pentagon said the United States and its coalition partners formally concluded “Operation Inherent Resolve,” while Washington said it would continue “targeted training and intelligence support” to Iraqi partners.
Zaidi said the end of the international coalition’s mission does not end the fight against terrorism, but shifts Iraq to “full responsibility for its security and stability.”

whatChangesNext.text: The pullout was agreed in 2024 under President Joe Biden and was carried out by Donald Trump’s administration.

In Gaza City, an Israeli airstrike on an apartment killed one woman, and an Israeli airstrike on a vehicle in Tel Al-Hawa killed at least four people and injured 14 others.
A strike near a mosque in Khan Younis killed journalist Mohammad Al-Najar, and a later Israeli airstrike killed one person near Qarara town.

The adviser said the warhead was designed to destroy high-voltage pylons and steel bridge structures and includes a 40-kilogram main charge and four additional destructive modules.

10545.title: US troops leave Iraq as mission ends

10569.title: Two children killed in grenade explosion in Lubero

whatHappened.text: Deux enfants ont été tués et leur père grièvement blessé lundi 28 septembre dans l’explosion d’un engin explosif à Lubango-Kilonge, dans le territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu.
Selon des sources locales, l’engin aurait été retrouvé dans un champ avant d’être manipulé par les victimes.
Le drame s’est produit dans une localité située à environ 17 kilomètres au sud-est de Kitsumbiro, dans une zone affectée par les conflits armés.
L’origine de la grenade n’est pas encore établie.

whyItMatters.text: Pour la société civile locale, cet incident illustre les risques liés à la présence de munitions non explosées dans les zones touchées par les conflits.
L’administrateur du territoire de Lubero plaide pour l’intervention des services spécialisés pour réduire les risques auxquels sont exposées les populations civiles.

whatChangesNext.text: La société civile appelle à une opération urgente de détection, de ramassage et de destruction des engins, ainsi qu’au renforcement de la sensibilisation de la population, particulièrement des enfants, sur les dangers liés à la manipulation d’objets suspects.
Les deux enfants ont été inhumés mardi 29 septembre.

10593.title: U.S. military completes withdrawal from Iraq after 12-year mission

whatHappened.text: The U.S. military completed its withdrawal from Iraq and vacated the last forces at Erbil Air Base in the Kurdistan Region, marking the end of the U.S.-led mission in Iraq.
The withdrawal ended Operation Inherent Resolve and closed the Iraq chapter of the U.S.-led counter-ISIS mission while shifting primary security responsibility to Iraqi forces.
CENTCOM said the anti-ISIS coalition work based in Iraq would move to Jordan as U.S. operations continued in Syria.

whyItMatters.text: U.S. officials said the change reduces the U.S role in addressing remaining security challenges in Iraq by placing primary responsibility on the Iraqi government, including threats from ISIS remnants and Iran-aligned militias.
The withdrawal also raised concerns that Iraqi Kurdish forces could face attacks by Iran and Iran-backed militias.

whatChangesNext.text: Final removal of personnel and equipment from Erbil completed the transition on Sept. 30.
The U.S. and coalition began leaving federal Iraq in October as Washington and Baghdad moved toward a bilateral defense relationship.

CENTCOM said the anti-ISIS coalition that had been headquartered in Iraq would now move to Jordan as U.S. forces continued counterterrorism operations in Syria.
Kurdish leaders have expressed concern that the U.S. withdrawal leaves them vulnerable to attacks by Iran and Iran-backed militias in Iraq.
The Kurds have been a close U.S. security ally and have also historically relied on U.S. protection.

Combined Joint Task Force — Operation Inherent Resolve remains active and is now headquartered in Jordan, according to CENTCOM. U.S. forces also continue counter-ISIS operations in Syria alongside coalition partners and the Syrian government.

10803.title: Assassination of social leader Gloria Buitrago and Camila Armero in Cauca

whatHappened.text: En Cauca fueron asesinadas la lideresa social Gloria Buitrago y la joven Camila Armero, con una diferencia de menos de 24 horas.
Gloria Buitrago fue atacada mortalmente en el corregimiento de El Plateado, Argelia.

Horas después, Camila Armero murió tras ser baleada en la mañana de este martes 29 de septiembre, cuando dos delincuentes le dispararon tras interceptarla mientras se movilizaba en su motocicleta en el barrio Villa Docente de Popayán.

whyItMatters.text: Los asesinatos son presentados como parte de una violencia sistemática contra las mujeres y los defensores de derechos humanos, y como una crisis de seguridad que vulnera el derecho fundamental a la vida.

10830.title: At least 32 children die in Balaghat district measles and malaria outbreaks

whatHappened.text: At least 32 children have died in India’s Balaghat district since May amid outbreaks of measles and malaria.
Officials attribute the deaths mainly to measles and malaria, possibly aggravated by malnutrition and delays in treatment.
The victims ranged from babies as young as three or four months old to an 18-year-old.

whyItMatters.text: The outbreaks are hitting remote families in Balaghat where reaching care can be difficult, and the losses are linked to multiple infections and delayed treatment.

11112.title: Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv flight: pilot stabs another pilot

whatHappened.text: A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv had an incident in the cockpit when one pilot stabbed another pilot on Wednesday.
Passengers and crew subdued the attacker, and the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk, in north-west Saudi Arabia, with all 174 passengers safe.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attacker “apparently tried to crash the plane”.
A passenger, Yaniv Hayon, said he helped stop the Omani co-pilot by grabbing the aggressor and pulling the controls.

whyItMatters.text: The incident prompted emergency handling of the flight and raised concerns about safety and possible motives while an investigation was pending.

11117.title: Ukraine war: Russia uses drone with warhead designed to cut power pylons

whatHappened.text: Russia used a jet-powered drone equipped with a warhead designed to destroy high-voltage power pylons and steel bridge structures for the first time, according to presidential adviser Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov.
Beskrestnov said the warhead was developed specifically to destroy high-voltage pylons and steel bridge structures.
The drone attack took place as Moscow renewed its large-scale campaign against Ukraine's energy system, launching a heavy combined attack on energy infrastructure overnight on Sept. 30.

whyItMatters.text: The Sept. 30 attack contributed to emergency power outages in Kyiv and nearby areas and in Chernihiv and Zhytomyr oblasts, according to the Energy Ministry.

11125.title: Morocco named first female prime minister: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri

whatHappened.text: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri was named Morocco’s first female prime minister.

King Mohammed VI appointed El Mansouri and asked her to form a government after her Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) came first in last week’s parliamentary election, winning 97 of the 395 seats.
El Mansouri said the appointment was “a truly historic moment” and that “for the first time in the history of our country, a woman is taking responsibility for leading the government.”

whyItMatters.text: The move makes leading the government part of a new political role for a woman, and it follows Morocco’s election results that put PAM in first place.
PAM will need coalition partners because it does not have enough seats to govern alone.

whatChangesNext.text: El Mansouri’s parliamentary seat will pass to the next candidate on her list.
She will remain mayor of Marrakesh until municipal elections scheduled for 2027.
In coalition negotiations, El Mansouri said there would be no “red lines.”

Поскольку онкологическое заболевание не исчезло, впоследствии женщине все равно потребовалось удалить и правую ногу, и в результате она осталась без обеих ног.

По его словам, перед началом хирургического вмешательства врач правильно отметил конечность, подлежавшую ампутации. Метка была нанесена именно на больную правую ногу.
